headline: PM Tarique Rahman to hold bilateral talks with Chinese Premier Li Qiang
summary: The meeting in Beijing will see the signing of multiple MoUs and the announcement of Bangladesh's first investment office in China.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to hold bilateral talks with Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Thursday afternoon.
The leaders are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding (MoUs), with some reports indicating up to 15 deals could be finalized.
A major highlight of the visit is the announcement of the opening of Bangladesh's first-ever investment office in China to attract more Chinese investment.
Prime Minister Tarique also sought Chinese support for the construction of the China-Bangladesh Friendship Hospital.
The Prime Minister is accompanied by a high-profile delegation including the Foreign Minister, Information Minister, and several key advisors on finance, education, and energy.
The official proceedings will conclude with a state banquet hosted by Premier Li Qiang in honor of the Bangladeshi Prime Minister.
caption:
Bangladesh is opening its first-ever investment office in China. 🇧🇩🇨🇳

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to hold bilateral talks with Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Thursday afternoon.

The leaders are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding (MoUs), with some reports indicating up to 15 deals could be finalized.

A major highlight of the visit is the announcement of the opening of Bangladesh's first-ever investment office in China to attract more Chinese investment.

Prime Minister Tarique also sought Chinese support for the construction of the China-Bangladesh Friendship Hospital.

The Prime Minister is accompanied by a high-profile delegation including the Foreign Minister, Information Minister, and several key advisors on finance, education, and energy.

The official proceedings will conclude with a state banquet hosted by Premier Li Qiang in honor of the Bangladeshi Prime Minister.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Somoy News

headline: Mexico thrash Czech Republic 3-0 to maintain perfect Group A record
summary: The victory secures Mexico's place in the knockout phase as Group A winners, marking a perfect run in the group stages.
details: Mexico secured a dominant 3-0 victory over the Czech Republic, maintaining a perfect record in Group A and advancing to the knockout phase as group winners.
The goals were scored by Mateo Chavez, Julian Quinones, and Alvaro Fidalgo, ensuring a victory in front of a roaring home crowd at the Azteca stadium.
The match also served as a emotional farewell for 40-year-old veteran goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa, who was brought on for the final 12 minutes of the game.
Ochoa, who made his senior debut at the Azteca in 2004, ended his World Cup career with a clean sheet in his sixth and final appearance.
Teammates and fans alike paid tribute to the legendary keeper, with Mateo Chavez describing him as an idol and an example of hard work and the league's experience.
Mexico now looks forward to the round of 32, where they will also play at the Azteca, hoping to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 1986.
caption:
A perfect group run and a legendary farewell. Mexico dominates the Czech Republic 3-0 to storm into the knockouts!

Mexico secured a dominant 3-0 victory over the Czech Republic, maintaining a perfect record in Group A and advancing to the knockout phase as group winners.

The goals were scored by Mateo Chavez, Julian Quinones, and Alvaro Fidalgo, ensuring a victory in front of a roaring home crowd at the Azteca stadium.

The match also served as a emotional farewell for 40-year-old veteran goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa, who was brought on for the final 12 minutes of the game.

Ochoa, who made his senior debut at the Azteca in 2004, ended his World Cup career with a clean sheet in his sixth and final appearance.

Teammates and fans alike paid tribute to the legendary keeper, with Mateo Chavez describing him as an idol and an example of hard work and the league's experience.

Mexico now looks forward to the round of 32, where they will also play at the Azteca, hoping to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 1986.
